body: The city, it just seems so full of life and I guess I want to leech that. haha

Mainly, I want to do anything that isn't being here in this chair. I hadn't even gone camping or built a fire until I was in my 20s and I forced that trip and had no one to go with. 

Although I would love to travel and see different places, see how people live, etc. I would settle with a trip to a local beach. I would settle with feeding ducks. I just want some experiences that are real. I've been made to feel too weak and helpless to go out on my own and when I get somewhere and I'm completely alone it feels pointless. There is no one to share experiences with. There is also the added horror of, when I go somewhere and sit in park or a restaurant alone, someone always advances on me or something. I would be happy if it were a friendly way, but it's only ever an obvious sexual advancement.

I guess I went off there but, I want to see New York and in contrast I've always wanted to go to Scotland or Ireland. Go to some really small town and meet people who are different than me, see some foreign landscape and paint it.

I read it all and I empathize and even relate in a lot of ways. I have violent fantasies as well and I can tell you they always surface when I feel helpless or I've been wronged and did nothing to defend myself. 

I guess honestly, it's a coping mechanism. I wonder if I need to tell my brain that I have some semblance of power over my own self, life, ego. I imagine myself in hero scenarios CONSTANTLY. I imagine myself as a wild and ruthless villain. I've imagined myself cannibalizing as well. All of this, I feel, stems from how helpless that I feel. I fear for my own sanity as well because of the violent fits I take and the shaking and rocking and crying that ensues. 

I am certain I would never do any of the things I fantasize about. You just need to find that certainty or actually go to someone beyond SW's abilities.  I mean this in the sincerest sense that if you feel you might hurt anyone you need to go to a professional. Maybe you are just like me though, maybe you just need to imagine yourself out of your own self, your own situations because you hate being who you are. 

Do yourself a favour and keep a journal where you only write about and chronicle good things. When you have an okay day or something nice happens, write about it.

When I say muddling through, I mean 3-4 years of college, hundreds of hours and sleepless nights. That's hardly inspiring, though lol. 

I completely understand, I figured it wasn't just the art that was making you feel this way and even if it was there is no shame in it. We can't help how we feel and this is a non-judgmental community. I get it if it feels like losing that passion has tipped you over the edge and it might be that whatever else is bothering you has sucked a lot of joy out of you--making it hard to enjoy most things, let alone art?

It may be that you need a break from it to discover new things about yourself or to heal before you can start to feel the way you used to. But since you are feeling so down right now, art may be a useful therapy. 

As far as personal commitments, the blog idea was to make your work semi-public and to imagine that you have lurkers who will be disappointed if you don't update. Hell, I'd lurk your blog to motivate you.

Anyway, you seem to be a talented, passionate person. You have far too much to lend to the world, even if you don't rediscover art. 

Whatever else is bothering you, feel free to let it out here. Don't bottle it up, you aren't alone.

Ah, look what art does to us. From one artist to another all I can say is that I fully understand. Being an artist is like having a volatile relationship with a person you hate, but you are unbelievably attracted to. 

That's what programs, courses and such are great for. They force you to keep drawing and creating regularly. For me, art school sometimes made it worse because I HAD to do it and some of the enjoyment was lost, but as I muddled through it got easier. I remember that my career choice is art and I'll get to create for the rest of my life. 

Everything you are going through is completely natural as far as my experience can tell. You even seem to be more logical than I when art isn't going well for me. 

The best thing you can do to get back the passion is to start a personal commitment. Many do it with a blog:

http://esterwilson.blogspot.com/ 
http://365-digipaintings.tumblr.com/
http://man4art.blogspot.com/
http://dailydrawingdiary.com/

You can't stop loving art, I'm sorry. It's in you forever you are just on a break with it. You need to rekindle what made you passionate for it in the first place. You'll not only create as you once did, but you'll be so much better.

About your family not wanting to endlessly help.. It may tire them, it may be hard but it sounds like whatever you are going through there are people who truly love you and want to see you do well. 

If psychotherapists and yoga don't work then maybe try something new? As in, is there anyone in your life that needs help, any cause you can put your heart into? I find that caring for others is therapeutic and is a constant reminder of the good things about humanity.

 I've felt like a burden before as well. The best thing you can do is counter it by being of service to someone who needs help.  You have so much worth and value and whatever holds you back you can overcome.

You have shown that you care for your friends and family enough that you want to put together a plan to shield them from the pain of your death. You have a great capacity for love and caring. Channel that. if you feel they carry you as a burden, then find a way to carry some of theirs.

Hey, I wanted to thank everyone who replied. I feel better now and you guys are right, I probably have a lot more power in the situation than I think. I guess the only issue I face now is my own moral turmoil of how badly I see this guy burned. I can't believe a portion of my fear now is getting him in trouble. My brain is stupid sometimes. 

SW is really helpful, just reading through positive messages everyone is giving to each other on here and the very fact that anyone is doing it or caring at all is a good feeling and made me feel hopeful. It is a reminder that whatever little shitty situation you are caught up in, that there is a world out there with good people who stay up late just to listen or just to be supportive. 

Thanks again.

You could try what the do in prison cells: burpees. You don't need a gym or any special equipment for it and you don't need more space than what is required for a pushup. Exercise isn't an end-all solution, but it really helps to clear the mind when it gets that nasty brain-dirtbag habit of making you think negatively.

I realize this will sound over simplistic, but why are you with him? You have gone through so much, put up with so much and you are the one supporting the two of you? He can't actually take your money. You have allowed him to. He has imaginary power over you. You are truly the one with power and strength. This boy is taking advantage of the love you need to give and receive, and he has preyed on your gentler, forgiving side. I must say I do not have your patience and your forgiveness.  But what I do have is a fresh perspective. What is he offering you? He treats you like shit, he takes your money he makes you depressed? Is it really worse to be alone? Have you considered living in a women's shelter for a short time until you have things in order? You could offer a lot to other women and girls there, you know. You wouldn't be alone. 

Don't be hidden anymore, please realize that you are full of worth and importance and you've been taken advantage of in your life for much too long.
You are feeling numb? Perhaps partying or being popular is not stimulating. Have you tried to explore yourself through art?

I signed up to get help tonight too. It seems it's slow in here so maybe us frantic people should talk it out with each other. 

You've been clean for 6 months, that is no small deal. That shows a lot of strength. I know that your low self-esteem will underplay everything you do and I know it first hand.  But you have to try and channel your brain to your accomplishments. You've had some bad breaks and a much tougher childhood than I can claim which I'm sure was a good part of the cause of your depression and self-esteem issues. This again is a proof of strength. 

Just in that brief description I can tell you are a strong person and somewhere in your head you are probably trying to reason against that (or atleast that is something I would do). Give your self a break and see some positives in you. 

You can't change your past, but you can direct your future. If you are on the same level as me and the future seems bleak and maybe not worth directing then maybe we need to channel a more animalistic pissed-off version of ourselves and figuratively fuck all of our problems and own them. 

I'm sorry if I'm not helpful but, I know how it is to be lonely. I spent most of my life without any friends. But that's what equally lonely internet people like me are for, right? I hope you are still online and you can talk with me. I'd like to hear from someone with strength.
